title: RaGEP: Rank-aware Geometric Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
claim: A two-stage coarse-to-fine procedure first allocates per-layer budgets by representation rank, then selects orthogonal high-energy components within each layer.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, with a circular zoom-in inset below
description: The figure reads left to right in three parts. On the left, an unpruned MoE model is drawn as stacked rounded boxes labeled Layer 1, 2, 3 ... n, each holding a 3x5 grid of dark squares that stand for experts. The middle holds Stage 1, Rank-aware Budget Allocation (Inter-layer). A feature-space matrix Σ_l feeds a curve of effective rank, with arrows to boxes labeled Preserved (High Rank) in orange or Aggressive Pruning in blue. The formula s_l = r_l^α sits on the curve. Below that, Stage 2, Spectral-Salience Pruning (Intra-layer), is a circular zoom-in. In it, redundant blue vectors are crossed out in red and orange orthogonal vectors are ticked in green. On the right, the RaGEP Pruned Model repeats the layers with only a few orange experts kept. Orange layers keep more experts and blue layers keep fewer.
caption: The overall framework of RaGEP. The process consists of two coarse-to-fine stages: (1) Rank-aware Budget Allocation (Inter-layer) adaptively determines the layer-specific sparsity budget based on the effective rank (Σl) of feature spaces, allocating more experts to information-dense layers; (2) Spectral-Salience Pruning (Intra-layer) selects experts that form a high-energy orthogonal basis by harmonizing Spectral Novelty (geometric orthogonality) and Activation Salience (magnitude intensity).
abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale model capacity efficiently but suffer from massive static parameter footprints, creating significant deployment burdens on memory-constrained hardware. Existing post-training pruning methods often rely on scalar statistics, ignoring the representational geometry of expert feature spaces. This leads to sub-optimal resource allocation across layers and the retention of redundant experts. To address this, we propose a Rank-aware Geometric Expert Pruning (RaGEP) framework to compress MoE models by analyzing the geometric properties of expert activations. First, in the inter-layer allocation stage, we introduce a Rank-aware budget allocation mechanism that adaptively assigns expert budgets based on the effective rank of layer-wise representations. Second, in the intra-layer selection stage, we propose a Spectral-Salience Pruning metric that harmonizes subspace orthogonality and activation magnitude to identify high-energy orthogonal experts. Extensive experiments across MoE models of different scales show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on a diverse set of zero-shot tasks, while reducing model size and inference cost.
